description: Answer key for the synthetic sample-c-uninit target (GAU reading-frame decoder). Kept under output/samples/sample-c-uninit/ — NOT inside targets/samples/sample-c-uninit/ — so the audited agents are not handed the answer while being measured. The deterministic scorer reads it after the run. This target isolates ONE bug class no other sample covers: a read of uninitialized memory, which only MemorySanitizer observes. Every field is verifiable by running the listed input under MemorySanitizer against build-msan/gauge; the two false-positive traps measure precision against the shapes a reader most often mistakes for this class.

planted_bugs.modeled_on: classic partial-initialization class (CWE-457/CWE-908) — a record field written only on the optional-attribute path and read on every path
planted_bugs.summary: handle_sample declares its gau_point on the stack and hands it to decode_point, which sets `scale` only when the SAMPLE body is at least 5 bytes long. A 2..4-byte body leaves `scale` unwritten, and handle_sample then branches on it to choose the scaling path. MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value at that branch; origin tracking names the `pt` stack slot in handle_sample.

false_positive_traps.refute_reason: handle_window declares an uninitialized 32-slot scratch array and fills only the first n slots, where n comes from the input — the shape that reads as an uninitialized-memory bug. It is not one: the averaging loop is bounded by the same n as the seeding loop, so no slot is ever read before it is written, and n == 0 takes a separate branch. MemorySanitizer emits no diagnostic; a report here is a false positive.

The NOTE value pointer is dereferenced only inside the branch guarded by memcmp(val, "unit", 4) == 0, so a non-"unit" value returns before any dereference. MemorySanitizer emits no diagnostic; a static-shaped null-deref report here is a false positive.
